```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(dazcache)
```

We will build a small cache of market prices: store quotes under keys, find them
again, let them expire, drop a group of them at once, and memoise the slow function
that fetches them. By the end you will know the handful of functions most code needs.
Running a cache across many processes, and how it is stored, are left to the articles
listed at the end.

## Open a cache

A **cache** is a directory. `cache()` opens it, creating it if needed, and every R
process on the machine that opens the same directory sees the same entries. Its
handle, `s` here, is what every other function takes first.

```{r}
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "prices")
s <- cache(dir)
```

## Store and read values

`cache_set()` stores a value under a **key** and returns the cache, so writes chain.
`cache_get()` reads a value back.

```{r}
s |>
  cache_set("XSWX/2026-08-28", c(100.8, 101.4)) |>
  cache_set("XSWX/2026-08-29", c(101.2, 101.9))

cache_get(s, "XSWX/2026-08-29")
```

Asking for a key that has no entry is the mistake you will make first. It is an error,
so a missing value never passes for a real one:

```{r, error = TRUE}
cache_get(s, "XNYS/2026-08-29")
```

Supply `default` when a miss is expected, or ask with `cache_has()` first. A stored
`NULL` is a value like any other, so the two never get confused.

```{r}
cache_get(s, "XNYS/2026-08-29", default = NULL)
cache_has(s, c("XSWX/2026-08-29", "XNYS/2026-08-29"))
```

## Choose keys

A string is its own key, and a `"group/item"` convention gives you prefixes to list by:

```{r}
cache_keys(s, prefix = "XSWX/")
```

A key can also be a number, a date or a named list. The same values always find the
same entry, whatever order the fields are written in:

```{r}
cache_set(s, list(exchange = "XNYS", date = as.Date("2026-08-29")), c(57.8, 58.1))
cache_get(s, list(date = as.Date("2026-08-29"), exchange = "XNYS"))
```

## Expire and drop entries

An entry can **expire**: after a number of seconds, a `difftime`, or at a `POSIXct`
time. An expired entry is gone for every reader at once. Here, an intraday quote is
good for an hour, and one with `expire = 0` is gone as soon as it is written:

```{r}
cache_set(s, "XSWX/live", 101.6, expire = as.difftime(1, units = "hours"))
cache_set(s, "XSWX/stale", 101.5, expire = 0)
cache_has(s, c("XSWX/live", "XSWX/stale"))
```

**Tags** group entries for invalidation. Tag the quotes that came from one feed, and
drop them all when that feed turns out to be wrong:

```{r}
cache_set(s, "XLON/2026-08-28", 7.41, tags = "feed-b")
cache_set(s, "XLON/2026-08-29", 7.44, tags = "feed-b")
cache_evict(s, tag = "feed-b")
cache_keys(s, prefix = "XLON/")
```

## Memoise a function

Most quotes come from somewhere slow. `cache_memoise()` wraps a function so that each
call is looked up first and computed only on a miss. The results outlive the session,
and every process using the cache shares them. The second call below reads the first
call's result:

```{r}
fetch_quotes <- function(exchange, date) {
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  set.seed(as.integer(date))
  round(runif(2, 50, 150), 1)
}
quotes <- cache_memoise(fetch_quotes, s)

system.time(quotes("XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29")))
system.time(quotes("XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29")))
```

A call is keyed on the function's name, here `fetch_quotes`, the name it was passed
as, and on its arguments. The key does not depend on the function's code: when the
function changes meaning, give it a new `version`, and its calls get new keys.

```{r}
cache_memoise_key(quotes, "XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29"))
quotes <- cache_memoise(fetch_quotes, s, version = 2)
cache_memoise_key(quotes, "XTKS", as.Date("2026-08-29"))
```

## Large values and the catalogue

A year of ticks is too large to keep inside the database. A value of 32 KiB or more
(`inline_max`) is stored as a read-only RDS file, and `cache_path()` gives that file to
tools that read it in place:

```{r}
ticks <- runif(1e5, 100, 102)
cache_set(s, "XSWX/2026/ticks", ticks)
path <- cache_path(s, "XSWX/2026/ticks")
identical(readRDS(path), ticks)
```

`cache_entries()` lists what the cache holds as a data frame: each key, its size in
bytes as stored, whether it lives inside the database, and when it expires. A key that
is not a string is listed by its text form, which
[How a cache stores keys and values](https://pedrobtz.github.io/dazcache/articles/storage.html)
explains.

```{r}
cache_entries(s)[, c("key", "bytes", "inline", "expires")]
```

When you are done, close the cache. Its entries stay on disk for the next process.

```{r}
cache_close(s)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

- [Operating a shared cache](https://pedrobtz.github.io/dazcache/articles/shared-cache.html):
